speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources for the past three years, what has been the number of recorded offences for (i) smoking in the common corridors and void decks of HDB flats and (ii) high-rise littering from HDB flats related to cigarette butts and cigarette ash respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: I urge smokers to be mindful of the health of others and not light up in smoking-prohibited places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Families and friends, and even members of the public, can help remind smokers to reinforce the right social norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: High-rise littering is an anti-social act which affects safety as well as environmental hygiene.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: I urge everyone to play his or her part to keep our common spaces clean and ensure that Singapore remains a clean, green and sustainable home for all of us.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The first is regarding enforcement of smoking in common corridors and also in stairwells.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I note the efforts of NEA, but I still receive a lot of feedback from residents about recalcitrant smoking in stairwells and common corridors, which is probably a bit difficult to enforce, particularly at odd hours of the day or even at night.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I was wondering whether there were any efforts to improve enforcement in these areas, perhaps using cameras that are already in some of the corridors put in by the Singapore Police Force.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second supplementary question I know is a common question.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We still have much feedback about second-hand smoke coming from the smokers' own residences.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And I know that the Senior Minister of State has replied on this.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But I was wondering if there was any update on any measures that we can take to mitigate this problem as well.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I am pleased to say that for the first question, at least I have an update.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is to enhance surveillance to curb unlawful smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But let me say that smoking is already prohibited in many, many places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I said 32,000-odd places, and actually, there are very few areas where our smokers can smoke now.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we are mindful about enacting laws that are too intrusive.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And, in fact, while many have given us feedback why do you not enact laws to prohibit smoking within their own homes, there are also many who tell us that they do not believe that the Government should intrude into one's private space.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we continue to encourage our smokers to be civic-minded and in the spirit of building a socially gracious and civic-minded society, I think we should all try to resolve this amicably, as far as possible.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How many are there and is there any in Nee Soon South?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, I have just given feedback to NEA over the last few weeks.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It looks like smoking in staircases is very, very common, and I received a lot of complaints.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Lately, there is this resident who keeps saying that the smoke goes into her flat and she has young children.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I have been talking to NEA, in fact, just last week.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are we going to have a national campaign about smoking at the staircase affecting the health of residents?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are there any installed in Nee Soon South?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Well, first, I would highly recommend that the Member start this social, civic-mindedness and gracious campaign among the residents, as far as smoking in residential homes are concerned.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, where there is persistent feedback on smoking issues in common corridors, lift lobbies and stairwells, we can look into the feasibility of providing such thermal cameras.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have no idea whether Nee Soon has any of these.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
